citation.authors: Scala I, Marotta J, Brunetti V, Del Tedesco F, Xhemalaj R, Rizzo PA, Frisullo G, Rollo E, Bocci MG, Piervincenzi E, Della Marca G, Maviglia R
citation.title: Analysis of the effect of 6‑Hz binaural beats on electroencephalographic and autonomic parameters of healthy individuals: An exploratory study

population.description: Twenty healthy adult volunteers, 10 men and 10 women (Methods 2.1: 'age range 25–53 years; mean age 31.35 years'; no SD printed, so sd is null). Screened by history: no medical, psychiatric or neurological disease, no CNS-active drugs in the 3 weeks before, no EEG abnormality. Recorded January 2021 to January 2022. Only the resting-state (BS) block is entered; the population is the whole cohort of 20.

protocols.name: rest_lying
protocols.description: Resting-state block (BS, the first of four blocks in the order BS, BB, MB, RN; no stimulation, played continuously with no interruption between blocks): lying on a comfortable bed with eyes closed, awake (Methods 2.1; the paper does not say supine). Block length: 2.1 and the Abstract say 'approximately 10 min'; 2.2.1 says each acoustic condition 'lasted between 10 and 12 min'; the mean artifact-free time analysed for BS was 657.7 +/- 79.2 s (2.3, EEG; the time analysed for the rate in 2.6 is not printed separately). The arm is therefore 10 min, the lower end of the stated range, and the window is minutes 0-10; the means may cover up to 12 min. The respiratory rate is the breaths counted over the analysed time divided by that time (2.6). No run-in before the block is printed. Fed state not stated and no meal is mentioned: the arm starts from typical values with no meal (norm_center, assumed; only heart rate and respiratory rate, which hardly depend on a meal, are entered). Clock hour not printed (10.0 assumed).

findings.description: Respiratory rate during the resting-state block (lying, eyes closed, no stimulation; block of 10-12 min, see protocol), mean of persons, mean +/- SD; the paper's unit 'count/min' (Table 2 row label) is read as breaths per minute, as its own definition of the rate is the count of breaths divided by the time analysed (2.6)

location.where: Table 2, 'Baseline' block, column 'Mean ± SD', row 'Respiratory rate (count/min)'

findings.description: Mean heart rate during the resting-state block (lying, eyes closed, no stimulation; block of 10-12 min, see protocol), mean of persons, mean +/- SD

location.where: Table 2, 'Baseline' block, column 'Mean ± SD', row 'Mean HR (bpm)'

left_out.what: Respiratory rate, heart rate, HRV, pulse transit time of the binaural-beat, monaural-beat and random-noise blocks (Table 2, the three later blocks; Results): these blocks are auditory stimulation, which the model has no input for

Baseline (resting-state) RMSSD, NN50, HF, LF and LF/HF (Table 2, Baseline block): the paper gives no meal or fasting state, so the HRV markers cannot be placed on a rest arm with the fed state unknown
